A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that a new aspheric intraocular lens (IOL) with an aberration-correcting design is capable of providing a high level of optical quality and contrast sensitivity.
we found that the IOLs were well-tolerated by patients with no serious adverse events and no significant change in the ocular parameters.

the use of an aspheric aberration correcting IOL in cataract patients with a preoperative high level of aberration is associated with a significant reduction of aberrations and a significant improvement of visual quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aspheric, aberrating IOL is a good alternative to the spherical, non-aberrating IOL in patients who have undergone cataract extraction and are not candidates for refractive laser surgery.

the use of an aspheric IOL in the presence of high aberrations may result in a significant improvement of the quality of the retinal image, and that the effect of the aspheric IOL may be even stronger than the effect of the high order aberrations.
the aberration correction provided by the Tecnis ZXR00 lens can be used for a broad range of patients, from those with low to high levels of aberrations.
